name: How Can You Tell If a Roofing Quote Is Too Low?

mainEntity.name: How do I tell if a roofing quote is too low to be real?
mainEntity.text: How do I tell if a roofing quote is too low to be real?

acceptedAnswer.text: A roofing quote is often too low when it looks incomplete. Common missing items include tear-off, new underlayment, flashing replacement, disposal, permit fees, ventilation work, and allowances for damaged decking. Some bids are intentionally low because the contractor expects to add charges later once the roof is opened. In Los Angeles County, that can be especially risky because older roofs may reveal hidden issues after removal. A legitimate low bid can exist, but it should still be detailed and explain exactly how the contractor can do the work for that price. The best way to evaluate a quote is to compare line items and confirm that each estimate includes the same scope and materials. If one bid is much lower than the others, ask what is excluded. If the answer is vague, the price probably is too.
acceptedAnswer.description: A quote is suspiciously low if it omits tear-off, underlayment, flashing, disposal, permits, or deck repairs. Some low bids rely on vague scope language and add charges later. The real comparison is whether the quote covers the same materials and labor as the others.
